name: ENet
reason: No numeric comparison against a named baseline in the repo (README only points to the homepage and gives build steps; repo page lists no benchmarks). The author's own mailing-list advice, seen only as a search snippet because lists.puremagic.com is blocked, is that TCP is probably the better choice for bulk reliable data, so no faster-than-socket claim exists. A snippet of an old scalability post (about 80k packets per second from 256 clients, said to exceed RakNet and ICE claims) compares against vendor claims, not a measured baseline, and could not be opened. Third-party .NET benchmarks cover the ENet-CSharp wrapper, not ENet.

name: FTP client for C++
listed_description: C++ client for making FTP requests.
reason: Thin C++ wrapper over libcurl; README (searched for benchmark, faster, perf, speed terms) has no performance claim of any kind, and a search for comparisons with curl or lftp found none.

name: GameNetworkingSockets
listed_description: Reliable & unreliable messages over UDP by Valve. Connection-oriented API (like TCP).
reason: README, repo page and release notes contain no numbers against a named baseline; the v1.3.0 notes say only that a fine-grained locking strategy greatly reduces lock contention (self-comparison, no figures, no baseline). Searches for GameNetworkingSockets against ENet, RakNet or TCP found no third-party benchmark. 10k stars, BSD-3-Clause, so a lead only if a benchmark surfaces later.

name: GNU adns
listed_description: Advanced, easy-to-use, asynch-capable DNS client library
reason: Project site (gnu.org) blocked by egress proxy; searches for adns benchmarks against c-ares or getaddrinfo found nothing (a c-ares mailing-list archive with a non-scientific c-ares timing was blocked and is about c-ares anyway). Also a DNS resolver, not an HTTP server, so the guessed category does not fit; belongs near event-loops-io or dns. No numeric comparison reachable.

name: gumbo-parser
reason: Repo is archived (2026-01-21) and says unmaintained since 2016. Its original README lists execution speed as a goal and its benchmarks/benchmark.cc only times parsing of local files, with no baseline and no numbers. Numeric claims exist only for derived projects: kovidgoyal/html5-parser (a variant of gumbo with a C lxml tree builder) reports 0.397 s vs 13.906 s for html5lib on a 5.7 MB document (35x with the lxml tree, 37x quoted), page https://github.com/kovidgoyal/html5-parser, docs/index.rst; that is evidence for html5-parser, not for gumbo-parser. Also not an HTTP server: guessed category is wrong (HTML parsing).
